DIMS employees compared each report with DIMS database records (GC–MS composition, physical characteristics, date and place of submission) of the tablet within 12 weeks before or after the report's date. Stated MDMA was scored too high or too low if more than 10 mg from the database value (for a range, its average); 'unreported substance' if similar database tablets in the window held substances the report did not mention; 'dangerous' if stated more than 40 mg too low (for a range, its average 40 mg too low or its maximum 40 mg below the database maximum) or if an unreported substance was psychoactive and present in relevant concentrations (not defined in numbers). The comparison rested only on the report's own information, so a poorly described tablet matched several distinct database tablets ('multiple database hits'), which the authors take to mean that several pills on the market fitted the description and a reader could not tell them apart from the report. All four authors are at the Trimbos Institute, which runs DIMS.
